To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) male parental activities at some breeding stages are correlated with paternity, (2) male participation in offspring provisioning is positively related to paternity, and (3) male participation in nest building, incubation and provisioning of offspring evolved as a consequence of paternity.
(1) male participation in offspring provisioning increases with high paternity and (2) male parental care is correlated among different components of parental care.
(1) paternity and male parental activities are positively correlated in birds and (2) this correlation is strongest for offspring provisioning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of paternal behavior and its relation to the evolution of mating systems.
the relationship between paternity and the evolution of paternal behavior.
the relationship between paternity and male parental care in birds, and with the evolutionary scenarios leading to the evolution of these two traits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
paternity has a positive influence on male provisioning of offspring and that this is a causal link.
paternity and paternal investment in birds are correlated, but that the direction of causality remains to be elucidated.
paternity is related to the evolution and maintenance of paternal care in birds, although it is not yet clear whether paternity is the cause or the effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evolution of paternal investment in offspring is not simply a by-product of the evolution of paternity, but is also influenced by other selective forces such as sexual selection.
paternity is a good predictor of male participation in parental care in birds, while the reverse relationship is not supported.
paternity is related to male provisioning of offspring, while other components of care are not.
The main takeaway from our work is that
paternity has a positive effect on male parental care in birds.
paternity and paternal investment are correlated in birds, and this correlation can be explained by the hypothesis that male investment in offspring is traded against paternity.
paternity is a key variable in the evolution of paternal investment in birds.
